newsitem.title: NORWAY: Derivatives trade rising on Oslo bourse.
newsitem.headline: Derivatives trade rising on Oslo bourse.

text.p: Trade in options and futures on the Oslo Stock Exchange has increased sharply since the derivatives system became electronic and a link was set up to Stockholm and London, the bourse said on Tuesday.
Daily trade in options and futures has gone up by an average 90 and 100 percent respectively so far this year compared to 1996, a statement said.
The new system, which links Oslo to the Swedish derivatives exchange OM and its London equivalent OMLX, went on line on February 14.
The statement said trade in Oslo, one of Europe's smallest derivatives markets, had increased both in terms of liquidity, number of players and derivative papers available.
"The Oslo Bourse expects the positive development to continue further once members of the cooperating stock exchanges become more active following the initial phase," the statement said.
In 1996, Oslo handled an average of only 6,000 contracts a day in stock options/futures and interest futures.
So far this year, average trade has risen to 9,565 contracts a day. In March alone, about 11,000 contracts a day were processed, a bourse spokesman said.
He said derivatives trade was mainly in stock options, which will total 10 companies as of Thursday when Den norske Bank ASA (DnB) and Petroleum Geo-Services ASA will be added to the options list.
The list also includes Aker RGI ASA RGI, Elkem ASA, Kvaerner ASA, Norsk Hydro ASA, Norske Skog ASA, Nycomed ASA, Saga Petroleum ASA and Bergesen d.y. ASA.
